Show events as they arrive, until Ctrl+C or --count of them. Good for checking an app's tracking
while you use it.

It starts with the latest few events, then prints each new one once. With --count it prints only
events that arrive after it started and exits once it has that many, so 'voidhash events tail --name
purchase_completed --count 1' waits for one purchase.

With --json each event is one line of JSON.

Usage:
  voidhash events tail [flags]

Flags:
      --count <count>       Stop after this many new events, such as 1 to wait for one
  -h, --help                Show help for this command
      --interval <Seconds>  Seconds between checks for new events (default: 2)
      --json                Print the API objects as JSON, for scripts
      --name <name>         Only events with this name, such as $pageview or purchase_completed
      --person <person>     Only events of this person: a distinct id, person id or email
      --project <project>   Project to act on: its id, slug, organization/slug or name (default:
                            this directory's project, then your default project)

Global flags:
  -d, --debug              Print each request and full error detail to standard error
      --no-color           Print without colors (also when NO_COLOR is set)
      --profile <profile>  Use a named config profile: its settings override the base config
                           (default: VOIDHASH_PROFILE)

Examples:
  voidhash events tail
  voidhash events tail --person user_42
  voidhash events tail --name purchase_completed --count 1 --json
